counterfactual_missing_items: Histopathology was negative for hyphae and neoplastic cells, and cultures grew no bacteria or fungi
An empirical course of prednisone (50 mg per day) for presumed trigeminal neuralgia provided no benefit
decisive_items: intracranial extension into the cavernous sinus surrounded the Gasserian ganglion
enlargement of the right sphenoid sinus with overdevelopment and opacity of the lateral recess
purulent discharge in the sphenoethmoidal recess
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete: it incorporates R1's sphenoid sinusitis evidence and adds the explicitly stated intracranial extension into the cavernous sinus. R1 captures the sinusitis but omits this major complication. R3 and R6 are contradicted by negative hyphae and neoplastic histopathology; R4 lacks steroid response and is overshadowed by sinusitis/pyocele; R5 is only a local operative finding; R7 is directly contradicted by prednisone failure and imaging findings.

rejected.why: Prednisone provided no benefit and imaging/endoscopy show sinusitis rather than primary trigeminal neuralgia.
Pyocele is a complication/finding of sinusitis, not the underlying diagnosis, and it omits the intracranial extension.
No steroid response and imaging shows sphenoid sinus disease with purulent discharge/pyocele rather than idiopathic cavernous granuloma.
Histopathology was negative for neoplastic cells, and imaging supports sinusitis/pyocele rather than a nerve sheath tumor.
Histopathology was negative for hyphae and cultures grew no fungi, so fungal invasion is not supported by raw findings.
